answer: Network-latency triangulation resists Sybil attacks by pinning agent identities to physical coordinates. Verifiers using synchronized crystal clocks send unpredictable nonces and enforce speed-of-light bounds, ensuring one host cannot harbor clones across an ocean or river basin. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of leasing dispersed hosts and links per identity. However, adversaries can route challenges via cheap regional proxies or pack Sybils in one metro zone below jitter limits.
